payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. Independent auditing corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The cell’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The dopant precipitates below 4 °C, requiring cycling to be suspended.
